newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end up higher, small caps soar.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end up higher, small caps soar.

text.p: Singapore stocks closed broadly higher on Wednesday, led by small capitalised issues and electronic shares.
"It was a strong close, all the indices are up and volume is also quite good," said a broker with a Singapore firm.

The surge in small was led by takeover target Asiamatrix, which surged to a new year high of S$1.93 before closing 19 percent, or 30 cents, up at S$1.90. The Sesdaq-listed counter is being taken over by three doctors.
The UOB-Sesdaq index closed at a new year high of 123.79, up 2.01 percent, or 2.44 points.

The SES Electronics index also closed at a new high of 123.79, up 2.01 percent or 2.44 points, led by gains in Aztech Systems, which rose 7.5 cents to S$0.61 and Amtek Engineering, up 16 cents to S$2.52.
An analyst with a British broking firm said electronic stocks were still in strong demand.
"The prices have run up very sharply but it is hard to call a sell on the sector, especially when prices continue to go up," he said.
Another broker said bank stocks were also in good demand on the back of an anticipated recovery in the economy.
The foreign tranches of banks DBS and OCBC rose 80 cents to S$20.50 and 40 cents to S$15.60 respectively.
Dealers said buying in selected index stocks like NatSteel and Fraser & Neave led the Straits Times Industrial Index to close 24.18 points higher at 1,974.69.
Total market volume was 270.77 million shares with 312 gainers against 87 losers.
